papers.title: Manufacturing Feasibility and Forming Properties of Cu-4Sn in Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Copper alloys, combined with selective laser melting (SLM) technology, have attracted increasing attention in aerospace engineering, automobile, and medical fields. However, there are some difficulties in SLM forming owing to low laser absorption and excellent thermal conductivity. It is, therefore, necessary to explore a copper alloy in SLM. In this research, manufacturing feasibility and forming properties of Cu-4Sn in SLM were investigated through a systematic experimental approach. Single-track experiments were used to narrow down processing parameter windows. A Greco-Latin square design with orthogonal parameter arrays was employed to control forming qualities of specimens. Analysis of variance was applied to establish statistical relationships, which described the effects of different processing parameters (i.e., laser power, scanning speed, and hatch space) on relative density (RD) and Vickers hardness of specimens. It was found that Cu-4Sn specimens were successfully manufactured by SLM for the first time and both its RD and Vickers hardness were mainly determined by the laser power. The maximum value of RD exceeded 93% theoretical density and the maximum value of Vickers hardness reached 118 HV 0.3/5. The best tensile strength of 316–320 MPa is inferior to that of pressure-processed Cu-4Sn and can be improved further by reducing defects.

summary_en.motivation: Investigate the manufacturing feasibility of Cu-4Sn via selective laser melting and the effect of processing parameters on forming properties.
summary_en.method: Single-track experiments and orthogonal design with ANOVA were used to determine optimal process parameters for high relative density and hardness.
summary_en.result: Cu-4Sn specimens were successfully fabricated with maximum relative density of 93%, Vickers hardness of 118 HV, and tensile strength of 316–320 MPa.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing including density measurement, hardness indentation, and tensile tests were performed to validate the forming quality.

papers.title: 大規模データ解析を目的としたCT画像からの大腿骨前捻角の全自動測定法
papers.abstract: Estimation of the shape and anatomical features such as anteversion angleof the femur provides useful information in total hip arthroplasty and femoral fracture treatment.Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is an operation widely used in orthopedic surgery which replaces a deformed hip joint with a metalic implant.Before the THA surgery, surgeons manually measure the femoral anteversion angle from CT image.Manual measurement is not suitable because it increases the burden on doctors and it makes the analysis with large-scale data difficult.Therefore, in this study, we propose an automated method for measuring femoral anteversion angle from CT image aiming for a large-scale population study.Using the proposed method, the femoral anteversion angle was measured for 100 CT images.The manual measurement by a surgeon was used as the gold standard data.The experimental results suggested correlation coefficient r = 0.872 for all cases, r = 0.826 for diseased femur, r = 0.926 for unaffected femur.Furthermore, we compared the automatic measurement results using automatically segmented femoral surface and manual segmented femoral surface for the analysis with large scale data.As a result, there was no significant difference.The usefulness of the proposed method was confirmed.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究CT图像自动测量股骨前倾角，虽与全髋置换相关，但未涉及假体应力遮挡或微动分析，对用户研究方向帮助有限。
llm.why_not_core: Does not quantify implant stress shielding, micromotion, or bone-implant interface mechanics; no FEA or biomechanical analysis of the implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 实现THA术前股骨前倾角的大规模自动测量
summary_zh.method: 基于CT图像的全自动前倾角测量方法
summary_zh.result: 与医生手动测量相关性r=0.872
summary_zh.validation: 以100例CT图像及临床手动测量为金标准

summary_en.motivation: To enable automated measurement of femoral anteversion angle from CT images for large-scale population studies in total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: An automated method for measuring femoral anteversion angle from CT images using image processing and shape analysis.
summary_en.result: The proposed method achieved a correlation coefficient of 0.872 with manual measurements by a surgeon, with 0.826 for diseased femurs and 0.926 for unaffected femurs.
summary_en.validation: Validated against 100 CT images with manual surgeon measurements as gold standard; comparison between automatically and manually segmented surfaces showed no significant difference.

papers.title: Acceleration of bone regeneration by activating Wnt/β-catenin signalling pathway via lithium released from lithium chloride/calcium phosphate cement in osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: By virtue of its excellent bioactivity and osteoconductivity, calcium phosphate cement (CPC) has been applied extensively in bone engineering. Doping a trace element into CPC can change physical characteristics and enhance osteogenesis. The trace element lithium has been demonstrated to stimulate the proliferation and differentiation of osteoblasts. We investigated the fracture-healing effect of osteoporotic defects with lithium-doped calcium phosphate cement (Li/CPC) and the underlying mechanism. Li/CPC bodies immersed in simulated body fluid converted gradually to hydroxyapatite. Li/CPC extracts stimulated the proliferation and differentiation of osteoblasts upon release of lithium ions (Li+) at 25.35 ± 0.12 to 50.74 ± 0.13 mg/l through activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in vitro. We also examined the effect of locally administered Li+ on defects in rat tibia between CPC and Li/CPC in vivo. Micro-computed tomography and histological staining showed that Li/CPC had better osteogenesis by increasing bone mass and promoting repair in defects compared with CPC (P < 0.05). Li/CPC also showed better osteoconductivity and osseointegration. These findings suggest that local release of Li+ from Li/CPC may accelerate bone regeneration from injury through activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in osteoporosis.

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the fracture-healing effect of lithium-doped calcium phosphate cement on osteoporotic bone defects and its underlying mechanism.
summary_en.method: Li/CPC was prepared and characterized; its extracts were tested on osteoblasts in vitro, and the material was implanted into rat tibial defects in vivo.
summary_en.result: Li/CPC enhanced osteogenesis and bone defect repair compared with pure CPC via activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.
summary_en.validation: Validation included in vitro cell assays and in vivo animal experiments with micro-CT and histology.

papers.title: Calcium Phosphate Bioceramics: A Review of Their History, Structure, Properties, Coating Technologies and Biomedical Applications.
papers.abstract: Calcium phosphate (CaP) bioceramics are widely used in the field of bone regeneration, both in orthopedics and in dentistry, due to their good biocompatibility, osseointegration and osteoconduction. The aim of this article is to review the history, structure, properties and clinical applications of these materials, whether they are in the form of bone cements, paste, scaffolds, or coatings. Major analytical techniques for characterization of CaPs, in vitro and in vivo tests, and the requirements of the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and international standards from CaP coatings on orthopedic and dental endosseous implants, are also summarized, along with the possible effect of sterilization on these materials. CaP coating technologies are summarized, with a focus on electrochemical processes. Theories on the formation of transient precursor phases in biomineralization, the dissolution and reprecipitation as bone of CaPs are discussed. A wide variety of CaPs are presented, from the individual phases to nano-CaP, biphasic and triphasic CaP formulations, composite CaP coatings and cements, functionally graded materials (FGMs), and antibacterial CaPs. We conclude by foreseeing the future of CaPs.
